definitions.explanation: Horse meat eaten as food. The name comes from the pink, cherry-blossom-like color of the raw flesh, and it is used in place of the plainer {馬肉|ばにく} on menus and in polite conversation.

examples.japanese: {桜肉|さくらにく}を{初|はじ}めて{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate horse meat for the first time.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{桜肉|さくらにく}の{刺身|さしみ}が{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: This restaurant is famous for its horse-meat sashimi.

examples.japanese: {熊本|くまもと}では{桜肉|さくらにく}を{食|た}べる{習慣|しゅうかん}が{昔|むかし}から{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: In Kumamoto, the custom of eating horse meat has continued since long ago.

notes:
A euphemistic name for {馬肉|ばにく} (horse meat), from the pink color of the raw meat. Restaurants and shops normally use {桜肉|さくらにく}; {馬肉|ばにく} is the neutral technical term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桜肉|さくらにく}の{刺身|さしみ}: horse-meat sashimi
- {桜肉|さくらにく}を{食|た}べる: to eat horse meat
- {桜肉|さくらにく}{料理|りょうり}: horse-meat cuisine
- {桜|さくら}{鍋|なべ}: hot pot made with horse meat

SIMILAR WORDS:
Animal meats have similar plant-based euphemisms:
- {牡丹|ぼたん}{肉|にく}: wild boar meat — from the peony-like arrangement of the sliced meat
- {紅葉|もみじ}: venison — from the autumn-leaf color
